verdict.rationale: Apple's own docs establish the two building blocks needed for local 70B-class inference — 546GB/s unified memory bandwidth (apple-m4-max-docs-20) and MLX's unified-memory array framework that lets large models run without CPU/GPU data transfers (apple-m4-max-docs-21, apple-m4-max-docs-35) — and Apple explicitly claims the M4 family lets developers 'interact with large language models that have nearly 200 billion parameters' (apple-m4-max-docs-2), which implies 70B-class quantized models are comfortably in range. However, missing for 10: explicit confirmation of M4 Max's max unified-memory configuration (only bandwidth is stated, not capacity), any specific 70B-quantized benchmark or tokens/sec figure, and independent/community corroboration of local LLM inference performance (community evidence only covers Geekbench/gaming, not LLM workloads).
